 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order
% 22.03.2023
1.
Pursuant to the previous order of this Court dated 13.02.2023, the petitioners have been exempted from appearance.
Respondent No.2 had been given option to appear through VC since she has delivered a child but she apparently is unable to be present.

2. This petition has been filed for quashing of the FIR No.1196/2018 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Aman Vihar, Delhi, on the ground of settlement between the parties dated 30.01.2021 arrived at with the facilitation of the Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

entities.text: Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 appears and states that respondent No.2 Ms. Neha has joined the proceedings through VC and confirms that all amounts under the settlement have been received.
The affidavit of respondent No.2 is also on record stating the same.
4. Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 were married on 20.10.2007 but due to disputes and difference, their marriage has resulted in a divorce.
One male child was born out of the wedlock.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.1196/2018 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Aman Vihar, Delhi, and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
